title: Beef, round, top round roast, boneless, separable lean only, trimmed to 0" fat, select, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Beef top round roast is a lean cut taken from the rear leg of a cattle. It is boneless, contains only the separable lean portion, trimmed to zero visible fat, and classified as "select" grade. Sold raw, it is commonly used for roasting, grilling, or making steaks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The top round is one of the leanest beef cuts, containing about 5 % fat.
It is traditionally used in dishes that require slow cooking to keep the meat tender.
In the United States this cut is identified by USDA code 5611, indicating its specific trimming and grade.
"Select" grade beef has a milder flavor and texture compared with "choice" or "prime" grades.
When properly seared, the top round can remain juicy despite its low fat content.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides roughly 22 g of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: With only about 5 % fat, it fits well into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin that support energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout or elevated uric acid should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium from processing
items.content: If the product is pre‑salted, consider total sodium intake in the diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The roast can be baked, grilled, slow‑cooked, or sliced thin for quick pan‑searing. Lightly season with salt and herbs before cooking. Raw beef is used in dishes like steak tartare or carpaccio, but only from trusted sources.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0–2 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container for 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for 6–12 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
